verdict: All ten scopes and full numbered/source-alias duplicate relationships pass in this bounded audit.
findings: Physical21 explicitly distinguishes one polyomino with translations/rotations/reflections from known planar translation-only decidability and multiple-prototile undecidability. Root D4 signed permutation matrices and grid translations describe the square-cell model. Physical19–21 Euclidean copies allow isometries, not scaling. Source periodicity is full-rank lattice periodicity; the root two-independent-vector formulation preserves it.

Current8October2026primary2610.12392 is a connected single TRANSLATIONAL3D polycube undecidability theorem; its abstract expressly says dimension2 translational monotiling is decidable. Primary2508.10067 uses FIVE planar translational polyominoes. Neither answers the one planar polyomino D4-isometry question. Arbitrary-polygon Einstein-type monotiles do not become square-grid polyominoes automatically.

Physical44 cardinality conjecture uniformly bounds dimension for EVERY integer tile with≤t points. The previous theorem allows dependence on coordinate magnitude/whole tile. The proof constructs positive coordinate-permutation copies, but the conjecture follows the source general Euclidean-isometry copy convention; root does not unnecessarily restrict permitted copies. Source reflection can be simulated in one higher dimension.

Physical48 defines copies of posets as induced subposets, so the root iff-order formula is faithful. Physical64 bounded-remainder question has arbitrary finite P, not just minimum/maximum posets. Tomon2018primaryTheoremA solves only the minimum/maximum case and actual finalConjecture4 retains the general finite-poset target.

Physical73–74 defines a line as the full intersection of the point set with an affine line having≥2 points. Physical78–79 two strengthened questions require many EXACTLY-l lines/no larger lines, or at least one exactly-four line in a sufficiently large set with no five-point line. Root uses maximal point-set intersections and retains all color/length quantifiers. Known cubic-curve counterexamples have no four-point line and do not refute these strengthened predicates.

Physical134 fixes an intersection when distinct domain subsets preserve their intersection CARDINALITY. Physical135 conjecture uses nonconstant self maps and n>2p. Physical151 distinguishes nonconstant maps into N^(p) from BIJECTIONS of[r]^(p). Root retains three genuinely distinct codomain/map-class targets and r≥p≥2. Degenerate one-element-domain cases are included as parameters to classify rather than silently removed. Sufficiently-large-r theorems are partial.

Physical129 exact F-edge problem counts an edge if it belongs to at least one noninduced F-copy, rather than counting copies or multiplicities. Root specifies all fixed finite simple F with an edge, every n,e and extremal graphs. Trivial edgeless-F cases are not a separate unresolved target. The exact triangle theorem for large n and dense three-chromatic asymptotics do not solve general F,n,e.

Primary1710.07255 explicitly refutes both old arbitrary vertex-transitive power and hypercube edge-packing conjectures, so those source historical statements are properly excluded. The punctured-interval result is likewise a solved proper special tile case. No complete closure of the ten exact accepted predicates was found in current bounded primary queries.
